cards.hearing: You may be hearing that tensions overseas, especially around Iran, got louder again this morning, and that oil prices jumped because of it.
cards.why: Oil feeds gas and diesel prices, and diesel is what moves trucks, so a jump there can eventually touch what things cost at the store or the pump.
cards.but: But a headline about a single tense morning is not the same as a reason to rework a long-term plan.
cards.story: Picture checking the weather and seeing a storm warning two states over. You might grab an umbrella, but you don't cancel the whole month's plans. Markets react to the forecast the same way, quickly and often temporarily.
say: We see the headline, and we're not rewriting your plan because of one tense morning.
Oil can jump without knocking your long-term plan off course.
